'Established in 1910, the Federation contained four colonial possessions' (Gabon, French Congo, Ubangi-Shari, Chad); infobox 'Established: 15 January 1910'. keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The 4 November 1911 agreement ceded part of the French Congo to Kamerun, which 'grew from 465,000 km2 to 760,000 km2'; 'The transfer took two years, and was completed when Ouham Region of Ubangi-Shari was transferred on June 1, 1913.' Germany gave France 'a strip of land in northeastern Kamerun near Fort Lamy between the Logone and Chari rivers'. Neukamerun is now german-africa's outline (Cliopatria 1911 minus 1905, fx-24, 1 Nov 2026), the region name 'Neukamerun' being absent from the gazetteer; the strip is drawn as a 100 km circle round N'Djamena (Fort Lamy), which overstates it on the Chad side.

ledger.note: 4 November 1911: the ceded Congo lands go to Kamerun. Neukamerun page: after Agadir 'on 4 November, they signed an agreement' by which France ceded part of the French Congo to Germany (Kamerun grew 'from 465,000 km2 to 760,000 km2'); 'The transfer took two years, and was completed when Ouham Region of Ubangi-Shari was transferred on June 1, 1913.' Dated to the agreement, as german-africa ledger gains Neukamerun on the same day and Cliopatria draws it German from 1911 (was 1 June 1913, the completion of the handover; moved by fx-24, 1 Nov 2026, so the two dossiers do not both hold the land in 1911-1913). The Neukamerun region did not exist in the gazetteer, so the loss never took effect; it now uses german-africa's outline (Cliopatria 1911 minus 1905).

region.text: 'a strip of land in northeastern Kamerun near Fort Lamy between the Logone and Chari rivers' given to France

ledger.note: 4 November 1911: France receives the Fort Lamy strip in the same accord. Neukamerun page: Germany gave France 'a strip of land in northeastern Kamerun near Fort Lamy between the Logone and Chari rivers'; german-africa dates its side to 4 November 1911 (Agadir Crisis page). The page dates the whole exchange (agreement 4 November 1911, handover completed 1 June 1913), not this part. The 100 km circle round N'Djamena overstates the strip on the Chad side (Chad is French anyway); only its Cameroon cells are new.

ledger.note: 1958 (September): the federation ends. The territories voted in the 'September 1958 referendum' to become autonomous within the French Community and the federation was dissolved; infobox 'Disestablished: September 1958'; Ubangi-Shari became the autonomous Central African Republic on 1 December 1958 and all four were 'fully independent in August 1960' (13 August 1960 for the Central African Republic).

notes:
Cliopatria has no French Equatorial Africa row; the colonies sit inside the French Africa aggregate (1846-1957). Every keyframe here is new and built from modern country outlines, which are soft claims for the Saharan north and for the Sangha-Ubangi lands.
Not settled: Chad's northern prefectures (Tibesti, Borkou, Ennedi) and the dates of their occupation (the French Chad page says only that the French 'gradually expanded into eastern and northern Chad'); Chad's status within the federation (colony 17 March 1920 to 30 June 1934, then unitary AEF in 1934 on the federation page, regions in 1934, territories in 1937); the formal return of Neukamerun (1916 seizure, the post-war line undated on the Neukamerun page; the French Africa dossier dates it 1919); the Vichy/Free French split of August 1940 (the federation page: 'most of the AEF rallied to the Free French in August 1940'), which is not drawn as a territorial loss because the federation itself went over to Free France.
Disagreement inside the federation page: 1908 versus 1910 for the division into four colonies. Infobox office-holders are partial (Merlin 1908-17, Chauvet 1951-58, Messmer 1958), so no ruler strip is given.
Gazetteer names needed: 'Neukamerun' (region: the lands of the French Congo ceded to Kamerun in 1911-13, mostly in the Sangha basin and western Central African Republic) and 'Dar al-Kuti' (region: northern Central African Republic). Counterparts: dar-al-kuti, wadai-empire (af-03-x/af-01-x dossiers), german-africa and free-french (Cliopatria rows).
